english.title: Fail to register a foreign activity arrangement
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having made a foreign activity arrangement, failed to register that arrangement with the Secretary of State before the end of the period of 10 days beginning with the day on which you made the arrangement, when you knew, or having regard to other matters known, ought to have known, that the arrangement was a foreign activity arrangement
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 65(5) and 80(1) of the National Security Act 2023.

english.notes:
(i) Section 67 provides complementary offences for those who carry out activities pursuant to unregistered arrangements under the enhanced tier. The activities in section 67 cannot begin until registration has occurred under section 65. Therefore, if this offence is committed and, a person has also carried out activities under section 67 without registration, further offences will be committed. See H101462 and H101462 for offences under section 67.
(ii) Section 68 provides a second set of ‘enhanced tier’ registration requirements under the foreign influence registration scheme. Section 68 focusses on activities conducted by specified persons themselves, rather those that they are directing through an arrangement that would need to be registered under section 65 and thereby fall under the remit of this offence. See H101464, H101464 and H101466 for offences under section 68.
(iii) Section 69 provides a requirement to register a foreign influence arrangement made with a foreign power. See H101467 for the associated offence under section 69.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 5 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction depends on the general limit in a magistrates’ court and may be 6 or 12 months depending on the date of conviction, see section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
